crossRefs.note: David put his hand in his bag, took a stone, and slung it, and struck the Philistine in his forehead. The stone sank…
David and his men went to Keilah, and fought with the Philistines, and brought away their livestock, and killed them…
David struck them from the twilight even to the evening of the next day. Not a man of them escaped from there, except…
Then all the tribes of Israel came to David at Hebron, and spoke, saying, “Behold, we are your bone and your flesh.
After this, David struck the Philistines and subdued them; and David took the bridle of the mother city out of the hand…
After this, the king of the children of Ammon died, and Hanun his son reigned in his place.
The people of Israel were struck there before David’s servants, and there was a great slaughter there that day of…
For the battle was there spread over the surface of all the country, and the forest devoured more people that day than…

parallels.note: I have consumed them, and struck them through, so that they can’t arise. Yes, they have fallen under my feet.

translations.web: I will strike them through, so that they will not be able to rise. They shall fall under my feet.
translations.bsb: I crushed them so they could not rise; they have fallen under my feet.
translations.kjv: I have wounded them that they were not able to rise: they are fallen under my feet.
translations.asv: I will smite them through, so that they shall not be able to rise: They shall fall under my feet.
